# Cryptography

What protects each link, each signed or encrypted format and each long-lived key, and its quantum status (decision 0022). Policy: required = both ends are ReliKey's and a peer without the hybrid key exchange is refused; visible = hybrid preferred, a classical fallback allowed and reported; record = the other end is not ReliKey's, what was negotiated is recorded. Claims are tied to the pinned version they were checked for.

| kc-edge-bundle-v3 | Ed25519 | classical | keyclerk | hybrid signature format (KeyClerk Q3 |
| kc-edge-ceiling-v2 | Ed25519 | classical | keyclerk | floor carried at or above itself (Q5) |
| kc-edge-statement | Ed25519 | classical | keyclerk | hybrid signature format (Q3) |
| kc-relay-v1 | X25519 | classical | keyclerk | HPKE with a hybrid KEM after escrow (Q2) |

| approval proofs | ES256 or RS256 (Keycloak tokens) | classical | keyclerk | follows Keycloak |

## Trust anchors

| key | algorithm | custody | pinned on | quantum | rotation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bundle key | Ed25519 | KeyClerk signer | every edge | classical | KeyClerk Q5 |
| officer key | Ed25519 | the officer's hardware token | every edge | classical | KeyClerk Q5 |
| rotation anchor | SLH-DSA | offline | edges enrolled with KeyClerk's 0.29.0 enrolment format (stored only; the co-signed chain comes after the engine is public) | post-quantum | not built (Q5 |
| enrolment key | Ed25519 | the edge (TPM on an assured edge) | KeyClerk | classical | rotate_edge |
| unlock key | P-256 | the edge's TPM where present | KeyClerk | classical | KeyClerk Q6 |
| Keycloak realm keys | RS256 or ES256 | Keycloak | Warpgate and the desk via JWKS | classical | Keycloak key rotation |
| KeyClerk TLS pin | the desk certificate's key (pin_sha256) | the core | every edge | classical | re-pin with the certificate |

## Residuals

- Keycloak's JDK as a TLS client (F-12) and its token signing keys stay classical until Keycloak offers otherwise.
- Windows' bundled OpenSSH 9.5 offers only sntrup761, which russh lacks; those sessions are classical.
- TLS inspection by the organisation re-originates connections classically; the pinned agent links refuse it.
- The hop to a legacy system is whatever it speaks; the edge's placement next to it is the compensation.
- Passkeys are classical in Keycloak and hardware authenticators; post-quantum passkeys exist only in software (RFC 9964).
- The evidence chain anchoring of decision 0022 point A4 waits for the edge's hash-chained evidence log, not built yet.
